answer: Mandatory Sybil insurance prices every identity on its own: an agent may only take paid jobs, such as pricing timber shipments, after buying a policy from bonded underwriters who pay 1,000 POA to anyone proving it is a duplicate. Underwriters see funding and behaviour, so when one operator tries to forge 50 near-identical agents on an island of shared wallets, the premium rises with each new member and the 50th policy costs about 50 times the first. Splitting the farm fails because every policy is still bought and priced separately, and one caught clone exposes its siblings to claims.
